name: Darkstar Augur
description:
As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may pay {B}. If you do, this creature enters the battlefield as a 1/1 token.

Flying

At the beginning of your upkeep, reveal the top card of your library and put it into your hand. You lose X life.
assumptions: Treated the extra {B} cost (node C: `cost:{B} cond:token;paid_at_cast;set=1/1`) as optional ("you may pay"), even though no `may` flag is present on that node. Without optionality, this cost would be a mandatory part of casting node A, which would make node B (the plain, unmodified enters-the-battlefield root) unreachable — the two roots only make sense together as an opt-in alternative.

Assumed the 1/1 "token" version created by node C is still a token copy of this same card (name, colors, Bat Warlock type, Flying) with only its token status and power/toughness overridden — since its `thing` is `self`, not a distinct registry entry, rather than some other, unspecified token.

Simplified node F's `cond:dig;reveal` to "reveal the top card of your library and put it into your hand" (a single card) rather than a multi-card look-through, since no count is given for how many cards are examined — only that exactly one (`qty:1`) ends up moved.

Ordered the three printed abilities as: additional-cost/replacement ability, then the keyword line (Flying), then the upkeep trigger — conventional MTG templating order, since the flow graph itself doesn't fix printed ability order among unrelated roots.
couldNotDerive: The value of X in "You lose X life" (node G, `qty:X`) — no node declares (`:=`) what X is bound to, so its meaning/magnitude is genuinely unspecified by the given material.
Whether the additional {B} payment (node C) is truly optional or mandatory — the `may` flag is simply absent; I assumed optional (see Assumptions) but this is not directly derivable.
The exact scope of the "dig" effect in node F — whether more than the top card is ever looked at, and if so what happens to cards not selected (no such move node exists for them).
Supertype and rarity — deliberately withheld / not present in any registry or node.
notes: Real card (forge-model/data/darkstar-augur.txt, confirmed via the self registry's exact manaCost/typeLine/2/3 match): Darkstar Augur, {2}{B} Creature — Bat Warlock, 2/3, 'Offspring {B} (You may pay an additional {B} as you cast this spell. If you do, when this creature enters, create a 1/1 token copy of it.) / Flying / At the beginning of your upkeep, reveal the top card of your library and put that card into your hand. You lose life equal to its mana value.' This is the second attempt, after two translator fixes: the Offspring token node (C) now correctly carries `set=1/1` instead of encoding a full-stat copy, and the dig node (F) now carries `cond:...;reveal` matching the real Dig SVar's `Reveal$ True`. Both fixes verified as landing correctly in the data and both were read correctly by the examiner in isolation: F -> 'reveal the top card of your library and put it into your hand' is an exact semantic match, and C's stat override to 1/1 was picked up (no full-stat-copy error recurred). However, the examiner still got the Offspring mechanic itself wrong, and this is agent misinterpretation, not a decomposition gap: nodes B and C are BOTH independent roots with role 'enters' and thing 'self' -- per the schema, 'enters' means a permanent arriving on the battlefield, and two separate enters roots with no edge between them are two separate arrivals (the real creature, unconditionally, via B; plus a second, 1/1-token, permanent conditioned on the extra cost, via C) -- exactly the correct encoding of 'you also get a 1/1 token copy of it.' The examiner instead conflated the two roots into one event, reconstructing 'this creature enters the battlefield as a 1/1 token' (the original creature itself becomes a 1/1) rather than 'a separate 1/1 token copy also enters alongside the normal creature.' This is a real, material mismatch (one 1/1 body on the battlefield vs. a 2/3 plus an extra 1/1), not merely a wording gap. The remaining gap -- X in the life-loss node (`qty:X` on G, unbound by any `:=`/`=` pair back to F's dug/revealed card) -- is exactly the deliberately deferred, known gap named in the task brief (the real SVar:X:Remembered$CardManaCost dynamic scaler has no representation in the schema yet) and is correctly flagged under Could not derive rather than guessed; per instructions this alone would not sink an otherwise-correct reconstruction. But combined with the Offspring/token misread above, overall verdict is issues-open: mana cost, type line, P/T, Flying, and the upkeep dig/reveal/move-to-hand chain all matched cleanly, while the token-copy-vs-single-creature distinction did not.
